_comment: VoIP handsets. Every enterprise number here was checked against the IANA registry rather than recalled — two I had previously left out as unverified turned out to be correct (Polycom 13885, Grandstream 42397), and one I might have guessed (Snom) is 7526 while 2338 is an unrelated company. itemtype is forced because a desk phone contains a two-port switch and so sets the sysServices datalink bit, which would otherwise classify it as network equipment. Identity comes from ENTITY-MIB, which is where handsets generally put it; phones expose very little else over SNMP.
name: Yealink phone

_comment: Cisco IP phones share Cisco's enterprise arc with every switch and router they make, so the sysObjectID prefix alone cannot separate them — the sysDescr regex is what does. Kept at a higher priority than the generic Cisco vendor entry so it wins.
name: Cisco IP phone
